Overview — The “Master Gland”

The pituitary (hypophysis) sits in the sella turcica and links the brain to the endocrine system. It is really two glands of different origin fused together:

🔬 Image slot — pituitary overview — anterior (adenohypophysis) vs posterior (neurohypophysis) with the hypothalamus
Anterior (adenohypophysis)
  • Epithelial/glandular; from Rathke’s pouch (oral ectoderm)
  • Makes & secretes 6 trophic hormones under hypothalamic portal control
Posterior (neurohypophysis)
  • Neural; a downgrowth of the diencephalon (neuroectoderm)
  • Stores & releases ADH & oxytocin made in the hypothalamus
Key split: the anterior lobe synthesises its hormones (glandular); the posterior lobe only stores & releases hormones made by hypothalamic neurons (neural).
How to Recognise Each Lobe on a Slide ⭐
🔬 Image slot — anterior pituitary (cords of coloured cells + sinusoids) vs posterior (pale nervous-tissue look)
Anterior
  • Cords & clumps of epithelial cells around sinusoids
  • A mix of colours: pink (acidophils), blue/purple (basophils), pale (chromophobes)
Posterior
  • Pale, looks like nervous tissue — unmyelinated axons + glia (pituicytes)
  • Pink dilatations = Herring bodies (stored neurosecretion)
Colour is the clue: a colourful mix of cell types → anterior; a bland pale “nerve-like” field with Herring bodies → posterior.

Mnemonic — basophils = “B-FLAT”: Basophils make FSH, LH, ACTH, TSH. The acidophils make GH & prolactin (“GPA” acids). Definitive typing needs hormone immunohistochemistry.
Hypothalamo-Hypophyseal Portal System (Anterior)
🔬 Image slot — hypophyseal portal system — hypothalamic hormones via median-eminence capillaries to the anterior pituitary
  • Hypothalamic neurons release releasing/inhibiting hormones into a first capillary plexus in the median eminence.
  • Portal veins carry them down the stalk to a second capillary bed that bathes the anterior pituitary cells — a rapid, private delivery route.
Hypothalamic hormoneEffect on anterior pituitary
GHRH / somatostatin↑ / ↓ GH
TRH↑ TSH (& prolactin)
CRH↑ ACTH
GnRH↑ FSH & LH
Dopamine↓ Prolactin (tonic inhibition)
Prolactin is unique: it is under tonic inhibition by dopamine, so stalk damage (loss of dopamine) raises prolactin while lowering the other hormones.
Posterior Pituitary (Neurohypophysis)
🔬 Image slot — posterior pituitary — axons from hypothalamic nuclei, pituicytes and Herring bodies
  • ADH (vasopressin) — made in the supraoptic nucleus; oxytocin — made in the paraventricular nucleus (with overlap).
  • Made in hypothalamic cell bodies, transported down axons of the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract, and stored in Herring bodies until released into capillaries.
  • Pituicytes are the supporting glial cells; there is no hormone synthesis here.
ADH → collecting-duct water reabsorption + vasoconstriction; oxytocin → uterine contraction & milk let-down. Failure of ADH → diabetes insipidus; excess → SIADH.
Stains
  • H&E — separates acidophils (pink), basophils (blue/purple) & chromophobes (pale) in the anterior lobe.
  • Hormone immunohistochemistry — the definitive way to classify anterior cells & adenomas (e.g. prolactin, GH, ACTH).
  • PAS — basophil (glycoprotein-hormone) granules; useful for corticotrophs.
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Prolactinoma
Commonest pituitary adenoma → galactorrhoea, amenorrhoea, low libido; treated with dopamine agonists
GH adenoma
Acromegaly (adults) / gigantism (children)
ACTH adenoma
Cushing disease (pituitary-driven hypercortisolism)
Non-functioning adenoma
Mass effect: bitemporal hemianopia (optic chiasm), hypopituitarism, headache
Sheehan syndrome
Postpartum pituitary infarction (the enlarged gland outgrows its supply) → hypopituitarism (failure to lactate)
Craniopharyngioma
Rathke’s pouch remnant; calcified suprasellar tumour in children (“motor-oil” cyst)
Diabetes insipidus / SIADH
Posterior-lobe/ADH disorders: too little ADH (DI, dilute urine) or too much (SIADH, dilutional hyponatraemia)
Pituitary apoplexy
Sudden haemorrhage/infarction of an adenoma → acute headache, visual loss, hypopituitarism
⭐ Exam Pearls
Anterior = glandular (Rathke’s pouch, makes 6 hormones); posterior = neural (stores ADH & oxytocin).
Acidophils = GH & prolactin; basophils = FSH, LH, ACTH, TSH (“B-FLAT”).
Anterior pituitary is controlled by the hypophyseal portal system (two capillary beds in series).
Prolactin is tonically inhibited by dopamine → stalk section raises prolactin.
Posterior lobe: ADH (supraoptic), oxytocin (paraventricular); stored in Herring bodies; glia = pituicytes.
Prolactinoma = commonest adenoma (dopamine agonist Rx); non-functioning adenoma → bitemporal hemianopia.
Sheehan = postpartum pituitary infarction; craniopharyngioma = Rathke remnant (calcified, children).
ADH problems: too little → diabetes insipidus; too much → SIADH.
